subtopic: Linear & Logistic Regression Assumptions and Residual Diagnostics
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #18: An online A/B experimentation platform detected anomalous metric movements and sample ratio mismatch (SRM) in Supervised & Unsupervised Modeling. In an active experiment evaluating 'Linear & Logistic Regression Assumptions and Residual Diagnostics', p-values were artificially deflated, and variance was underestimated by 60%.

### Engineering Challenge:
Which statistical remediation correctly eliminates false positive statistical significance in this 'Linear & Logistic Regression Assumptions and Residual Diagnostics' evaluation?

options.text: Run standard two-sample independent t-tests treating every individual page event as an independent observation.
Apply cluster-robust standard errors or Delta method variance corrections to account for intra-cluster correlation across repeated user sessions.
Drop all users who logged in more than once during the experimental trial window.
Increase the alpha threshold from 0.05 to 0.20 to accept the observed metric variance.

answer_explanation: In Supervised & Unsupervised Modeling, analyzing session-level observations when randomization occurs at the user level introduces intra-cluster correlation. Using naive standard errors severely underestimates variance. Cluster-robust variance estimators or the Delta method restore nominal false positive rates.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option B. Rationale: In Supervised & Unsupervised Modeling, analyzing session-level observations when randomization occurs at the user level introduces intra-cluster correlation. Using naive standard errors severely underestimates variance. Cluster-robust variance estimators or the Delta method restore nominal false positive rates.
